MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Urine (ThinPrep)
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Elderly male patient with bladder tumor and left ureter filling defect. Recent urine cytology (Paris category 3) suggests possible instrumentation effect or low grade urothelial carcinoma. FISH analysis requested to evaluate for chromosomal abnormalities associated with bladder cancer.

TEST PERFORMED
UroVysion Bladder Cancer Kit (GeneTech BCA-300)
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) analysis

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was attempted using the FDA-approved UroVysion Bladder Cancer Kit on ThinPrep-processed urine specimen. This multi-target, multicolor FISH probe set is designed to detect aneuploidy for chromosomes 3, 7, 17, and loss of the 9p21 locus.

Probe Set:
- CEP3 (SpectrumRed): Chromosome 3 centromere
- CEP7 (SpectrumGreen): Chromosome 7 centromere
- CEP17 (SpectrumAqua): Chromosome 17 centromere
- LSI 9p21 (SpectrumGold): 9p21 locus

RESULT
TEST FAILED - INSUFFICIENT CELLULAR MATERIAL

The ThinPrep slide contained insufficient urothelial cells for FISH analysis. Multiple areas of the slide were examined, but adequate numbers of morphologically abnormal cells required for UroVysion scoring criteria could not be identified. A minimum of 25 morphologically abnormal cells is required for analysis per manufacturer guidelines.

Cells observed: <5 urothelial cells identified
Analysis: Not performed due to insufficient cellularity

INTERPRETATION
FISH assessment for bladder cancer-associated chromosomal abnormalities could not be performed due to insufficient cellular material on the ThinPrep slide. This technical failure prevents evaluation of aneuploidy patterns that would aid in the detection and monitoring of bladder cancer.

LIMITATIONS
The UroVysion test requires adequate cellularity with morphologically abnormal cells for accurate interpretation. Low cellularity samples may result in false-negative results or test failure as occurred in this case.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Consider repeat urine collection with attention to:
- First morning void specimen preferred
- Adequate hydration prior to collection
- Collection of sufficient volume (minimum 50 mL)
- Prompt processing to preserve cellular integrity

Alternative testing options include repeat cystoscopy with directed biopsy or enhanced cystoscopy techniques.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
